CO Source Characteristics 2 The CO 2 fermentation scrubber from OEE’s ethanol fermenters provides the source CO 2 for this project. The compression and dehydration facility will be designed to operate based on the feed composition given in Table 3 below. The typical feed composition in Table 3 is based on a series of twelve bag measurements made by Airborne Labs International for OEE. The measured oxygen concentrations ranged from 14 to 1300 ppmv. Table 3 also shows the assumed feed composition for the FEED work. Table 3. Typical CO 2 Source Composition. Additional trace impurities such as ethanol and acetaldehyde may be present in the feed gas, but the CO 2 recovery facility will not be designed to remove them. The concentration of oxygen and nitrogen in the feed gas depends upon the sequence of operation in the upstream fermenters, as these impurities arise from air in-leakage. CO Production Specifications 2 The production of injection grade CO2 only requires the removal of water prior to injection. The water limit in the injected CO2 is 30 lb/MMscf (633 ppmv), but a typical treatment specification of 10 lb/MMscf (211 ppmv) will be used. Other impurities in the source CO , including oxygen, are not 2 removed at the facility. Process Capacity and Delivery Requirements The injection and dehydration system will be sized to process the entire feed stream from the OEE plant fermenters, but this does not equate to recovering 100% of the CO 2 fed to the facility.
